references.name: Irving Fisher
references.desc: Fisher equation (nominal = real + inflation); “impatience and opportunity” theory of interest; dedicated Theory of Interest to Böhm-Bawerk and John Rae

references.name: John Maynard Keynes
references.desc: Liquidity-preference theory (1936); three motives for money demand (transactions, precautionary, speculative); interest rates as “purely a monetary phenomenon”

references.name: Knut Wicksell
references.desc: Natural rate of interest concept; loanable funds theory precursor; cumulative process: divergence between market and natural rate causes inflation/deflation

references.name: Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk
references.desc: Time-preference theory (1889); three reasons for positive time preference; “roundaboutness” concept—indirect production yields higher productivity

references.name: John Rae
references.desc: First linked time preference and productivity of capital; Scottish-American economist foundational to interest rate theory

references.name: Frederick Macaulay
references.desc: Duration measure (1938)—weighted average time to receive cash flows, foundational to all modern duration concepts

references.name: F.M. Redington
references.desc: Immunization theory (1952)—matching asset and liability durations to protect against interest rate changes

references.name: Thomas Ho
references.desc: Key rate duration (1992)—11 specific maturities on the Treasury spot rate curve for measuring non-parallel yield curve sensitivity

references.name: Donald Chambers & Willard Carleton
references.desc: Duration vectors (1988)—predecessors to key rate duration, measuring sensitivity to multiple maturity points

references.name: Robert Reitano
references.desc: Partial durations (series of papers); demonstrated classical immunization can disguise risks from non-parallel yield curve shifts

references.name: Robert Merton / Fischer Black / Myron Scholes
references.desc: Option pricing model; Merton’s structural model treats equity as call option on firm assets; Black-Scholes has three critical limitations for bonds

references.name: Black, Derman & Toy
references.desc: Arbitrage-free binomial interest-rate model for valuing bonds with embedded options; rate evolution as lognormal: rH = rL × e2σ

references.name: Edward Altman
references.desc: Default prediction models; recovery rate estimation; Z-score for bankruptcy prediction; cumulative default rate research

references.name: Gifford Fong & Oldrich Vasicek
references.desc: M-squared measure of immunization risk; multi-period immunization conditions; quantifying cash flow dispersion risk

references.name: Jarrow-Turnbull / Duffie-Singleton
references.desc: Reduced-form credit risk models; default as exogenous Poisson process; quickly calibrate to market spreads; favored by 90%+ of practitioners

references.name: Giesecke & Goldberg
references.desc: Incomplete-information credit model combining structural/reduced-form approaches; investors don’t know default barrier, accounting for corporate fraud; used by MSCI Barra

references.name: Andrew Davidson & Michael Levin
references.desc: MBS analytics; identified OAS constancy problem for IO/PO/pass-through parity

references.name: Douglas Breeden
references.desc: Coupon curve duration—market-based duration using roll-up/roll-down along the coupon curve

references.name: Klaffky, Ma & Nozari
references.desc: Yield curve reshaping duration framework: SEDUR and LEDUR for short-end and long-end sensitivity

references.name: Li & Zhang
references.desc: Truncated index studies showing loser avoidance > winner selection for credit; credit risk model (gamma) strategies

references.name: Stefanini
references.desc: Taxonomy of eight convertible bond arbitrage strategies: cash flow, volatility, gamma, delta, and others

references.name: Gary Gorton
references.desc: Safe asset definition: “an asset that is (almost always) valued at face value without expensive and prolonged analysis”—central to the safe asset controversy

references.name: Ferreira & Shousha
references.desc: Study (1970–2018) showing 20% of natural rate variance explained by net supply of sovereign safe assets; global accumulation reduced rates by 50bps

references.name: Dennis Robertson & Bertil Ohlin
references.desc: Developed loanable funds theory in 1930s, extending Wicksell’s work to include financial intermediaries, government demand, and cash holdings

references.name: Paul Volcker
references.desc: Fed chairman 1979–1987; series of tightenings to 20%+ fed funds rate to break inflation; caused two recessions but restored price stability

references.name: Mark Carney
references.desc: Bank of England governor/FSB chair; promoted green bonds: “development of green bonds is opportunity to advance low carbon future while raising global investment”

references.name: Knut Kjaer
references.desc: Founding CEO, Norges Bank Investment Management (Norway sovereign wealth fund); argued debt markets give investors greater climate impact than equity markets

references.name: Christian Kopf
references.desc: Head of fixed income, Union Investment; proposed carbon policy performance bonds (CPPBs) using covenant mechanisms to enforce emission targets

references.name: Ng & Phelps
references.desc: Constraint-tolerant investing research (1990–2009); showed retaining fallen angels and maturity/liquidity violators consistently outperformed strict index replication

references.name: Ben Dor & Xu
references.desc: Documented fallen angel outperformance of 6.63% over two years post-downgrade; showed price pressure from forced selling creates systematic alpha opportunity

references.name: John Finnerty
references.desc: Extended binomial model to incorporate default risk for non-investment-grade bonds with multiple embedded options; applied to Bucyrus-Erie pay-in-kind debenture

references.name: Hilscher & Wilson
references.desc: Demonstrated credit ratings are inaccurate default probability measures; simple reduced-form models consistently outperform agency ratings for forecasting corporate failure

references.name: Kamakura Corporation
references.desc: Applied reduced-form credit models to 431 Bank of America bonds, finding BAC’s 15 issues ranked in the bottom 17% on return-risk criterion—demonstrating that heavily traded names can be poor relative value

references.name: Litterman & Scheinkman
references.desc: Factor decomposition of Treasury returns: 91.6% from parallel shifts (level), 5.0% from twists (slope), 3.4% from butterfly movements (curvature)—foundational for yield curve risk management

references.name: Marco López de Prado
references.desc: Advanced backtesting methodologies with four advantages of Monte Carlo simulation over walk-forward; identified key biases: survivorship, look-ahead, and optimal period bias

references.name: Felix Goltz
references.desc: Smart beta research for fixed income: argued minimum-volatility bond strategies simply concentrate in short-duration high-quality issues, concluding “there’s a long way to go before smart beta can become a reality for fixed-income portfolios”

references.name: Goltz & Campani
references.desc: Study (1997–2010) showing cap-weighted IG bond indexes are “fairly unstable” in risk exposures—sector weights and durations shift as issuance patterns change, undermining the benchmark’s representativeness

references.name: Ronald Ryan
references.desc: Liability-driven investing pioneer who proposed using only Treasury STRIPS to match projected liabilities exactly, eliminating reinvestment risk entirely since STRIPS have no intermediate coupon payments
